Migrating to synapser 3.0

2026-11-25

Source: vignettes/migration_to_synapser_3_0.Rmd
migration_to_synapser_3_0.Rmd

Who this guide is for

This guide is for anyone with existing R code that uses synapser 2.x. Upgrading to 3.0 will break that code: functions have been renamed, arguments have new names, and the objects you get back are structured differently.

The good news is that the code fails with a clear error rather than silently returning wrong results. Typical errors look like this:

  • could not find function "synTableQuery" (a renamed or removed function)
  • unused argument (parentId = "syn123") (an argument now in snake_case)
  • AttributeError: 'File' object has no attribute 'properties' (a property that is no longer nested under $properties)

If you’re writing new code rather than porting old code, you don’t need this guide at all: start from Data Upload, Download, and Delete and Tables.

Why upgrade now

Staying on 2.x costs you more than the new API:

  • Frozen R dependencies. 2.x pins reticulate to 1.25–1.28 and rjson to ≤ 0.2.21, which holds back every other project sharing your R library. 3.0 drops both ceilings.
  • A Python ceiling. 2.x supports only Python 3.9–3.11 (with old pandas and numpy caps). 3.0 supports Python 3.11–3.15 and no Python setup is needed.
  • An outdated Python client. 2.x is stuck on synapseclient 4.4.2. 3.0 is built on 4.15, and new Python client features become available in R as soon as they are released. See What you gain in 3.0.

Why this release is not backwards compatible

Previous versions of synapser wrapped a hand-curated subset of the Python client behind R-idiomatic function names and camelCase arguments. 3.0 upgrades the reticulate/rjson dependency and keep pace with the Python client’s newer synapseclient.models/synapseclient.operations architecture, generates the R layer directly from those Python OOP models instead of maintaining a separate hand-written wrapper. The result is an API that mirrors the Python client field-for-field, so most existing synapser scripts will need updates.

This guide covers the Project/Folder/File/Table workflow — the paths most scripts use. The same patterns apply to every other entity type (Dataset, Views, Evaluation, Team, Wiki, …); see the full reference for exact signatures.

What you gain in 3.0

Upgrading costs a round of script updates (see below), but it buys you real capability, not just a version bump:

  • No Python environment to manage, and no pinned dependencies. synapser sets up the Python client it needs the first time it loads, so there is no virtualenv to create, activate, or repair by hand. Its R dependencies (reticulate, rjson) are no longer held to old versions, so installing synapser doesn’t force older packages on the rest of your R library.
  • New functionality that 2.x simply didn’t have. Recursive synCopy()/synSyncFromSynapse()/synWalk(), manifest-driven bulk upload (synGenerateSyncManifest()/synSyncToSynapse()), hierarchy-wide synListAcl() and synDeletePermissions() (with a dry_run preview), and JSON Schema binding/validation (synBindSchema(), synValidateSchema(), …), table upserts (synUpsertRows()), wiki history and restore, functions for running evaluation queues, and Synapse AI agent chat are all new in 3.0. See New in 3.0: capabilities that didn’t exist before below.
  • New entity types, not just new methods on the old ones. VirtualTable, DatasetCollection, Agent/AgentSession, and Organization/JSONSchema have no 2.x counterpart at all, and the view types (EntityView, MaterializedView, SubmissionView) replace 2.x’s EntityViewSchema/MaterializedViewSchema/SubmissionViewSchema while picking up the same column, query, and ACL verbs as Table.
  • Faster access to new Python client features going forward. Because the R layer is generated from the same OOP models the Python client ships, new methods and arguments added to synapseclient can be surfaced in R without waiting on a hand-written wrapper to catch up.
  • One mental model, matching the Python docs. Every entity — File, Folder, Table, Dataset, Project, … — now follows the same Constructor(...) |> synMethod(...) shape, with snake_case arguments that match the Python client’s field names exactly.
  • Comprehensive documentation. Every entity and every function has its own reference page with R examples, organized by entity type on the reference site. Beyond the reference, there are step-by-step tutorials for each entity type (Projects, Folders, Files, Tables, Views, Datasets, Wikis, Evaluations, Submissions, …), workflow guides for tasks such as bulk upload and download and sharing settings, and concept articles on Synapse’s data model, access control, and annotations. See Where to go next for the full list.

In short, upgrading to 3.0 means updating your scripts once. In return, you get no Python setup and no pinned dependencies, much broader Synapse coverage (new entity types plus recursive, bulk-upload, and schema workflows), one consistent API that matches the Python client, and full documentation for every entity and function. Because the R layer is generated from the Python client, it stays current as the Python client evolves.

Before you upgrade

synapser 3.0 requires:

  • R 4.2.0 or later.
  • reticulate 1.44.0 or later. Earlier versions, including the 1.28 that 2.x pinned, fail with could not find a Python environment for /.
  • Python 3.11 to 3.15. Synapser downloads a compatible Python and the Synapse Python client into its managed environment the first time synapser loads.

If you set up pinned dependencies for 2.x (such as rjson and reticulate), remove them, and remove the r-reticulate virtualenv and any RETICULATE_PYTHON setting so synapser can use its managed environment via uv. Then restart R:

install.packages(c("rjson", "reticulate"))
reticulate::virtualenv_remove("r-reticulate")

Run reticulate::py_config() to check which Python synapser is using. See Installation for details.

Four patterns to relearn

1. Instance-first, then pipe

Every entity is now a real object you construct directly — File(...), Folder(...), Table(...), Project(...), … — and every operation on it is a “verb” function (synStore(), synGet(), synSetProperties(), synAddColumn(), synDeleteRows(), …) that takes the instance as its first argument. You construct the object first, then thread it through a chain of these verbs with the native pipe, tidyverse-style, instead of reassigning a variable at every step:

# 2.x -- synStore() was one Python-backed function shared by every entity
# type, with Python duck-typing on `obj` internally; each step reassigned a
# variable rather than chaining
file <- File(path, parentId = "syn123")
file <- synStore(file)
file <- synGet(file$properties$id, downloadFile = FALSE)

# 3.0 -- construct the instance, then pipe it through verbs
file <- File(path = path, parent_id = "syn123") |>
  synStore() |>
  synGet(file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE))

This is the change everything else in this guide follows from. Two kinds of function take an instance this way:

  • synStore(), synGet(), and synDelete() are single factory functions that accept any supported entity — or, for synGet() and synDelete(), a Synapse ID string instead — and apply the behavior appropriate to that entity’s type.
  • Every other verb (synAddColumn(), synGetAcl(), synCopy(), synWalk(), synBindSchema(), …) is a generic that dispatches on the class of the object you pipe in. The same verb name therefore works uniformly across every entity type that supports it.

2. Properties are no longer nested under $properties and synSetProperties

Properties and annotations are now plain fields on the object. Read them directly, and update them with the convenience function synSetProperties(), which sets any number of fields, including annotations, in one call and returns the entity so you can pipe it into synStore():

# 2.x
entity$properties$id
entity$properties$name
entity$annotations$assay

# 3.0
entity$id
entity$name
entity$annotations$assay

synGet(synapse_id) |>
  synSetProperties(
    name = "new name",
    version_label = "2",
    annotations = list(assay = "RNA-seq")
  ) |>
  synStore()

Setting annotations replaces all of the entity’s existing annotations. To add to them instead, combine them first: synSetProperties(annotations = append(entity$annotations, list(key = "value"))).

3. Arguments are snake_case, matching the Python client exactly 

# 2.x
synGet(entity, downloadFile = FALSE)
synStore(obj, forceVersion = FALSE, versionLabel = "2")
File(path, parentId = project$properties$id)

# 3.0
synGet(entity, file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE))
obj |> synSetProperties(force_version = FALSE, version_label = "2") |> synStore()
File(path = path, parent_id = project$id)

Some arguments didn’t just change case; they moved. In 2.x, forceVersion and versionLabel were arguments to synStore(). In 3.0 they are fields on the entity (force_version, version_label), which you set when you create the entity or with synSetProperties(). synStore() no longer accepts them. It takes only the entity, an optional parent, and an options object for the entity type, such as StoreFileOptions(), StoreContainerOptions(), or StoreTableOptions().

4. Property Mutation goes through synSetProperties(), then an explicit synStore()

Directly assigning into $properties no longer works. Properties are set with synSetProperties() — which validates the field names against the object’s dataclass fields — and piped into synStore():

# 2.x
entity$properties$name <- "new name"
entity <- synStore(entity)

# 3.0
entity <- synGet(synapse_id) |>
  synSetProperties(name = "new name") |>
  synStore()

Table columns are the one exception — those are still mutated in place on the $columns list before synStore():

table$columns[["Expression"]]$name <- "Expression2"
table$columns[["Expression"]]$column_type <- "INTEGER"
table |> synStore()

The column verbs synAddColumn(), synDeleteColumn(), and synReorderColumn() work the same way: they change the table object in place and return nothing, so they are separate statements rather than links in a pipe into synStore():

table |> synAddColumn(Column(name = "Expression", column_type = "STRING"))
table |> synStore()

Side-by-side reference: common operations

Task 2.x (legacy) 3.0 (new)
Create + store an entity File(path, parentId = "syn123") then synStore(obj) File(path = path, parent_id = "syn123") \|> synStore()
Suppress a new version synStore(obj, forceVersion = FALSE) File(path = path, parent_id = "syn123", force_version = FALSE) \|> synStore()
Set name / version label entity$properties$name <- "x"; synStore(entity) synGet(id) \|> synSetProperties(name = "x") \|> synStore()
Move an entity synMove(entity, newParent) synGet(id) \|> synSetProperties(parent_id = "syn456") \|> synStore()
Track provenance synStore(obj, used = "syn123", executed = "syn456") synGet(id) \|> synSetProperties(activity = Activity(used = list(UsedEntity(target_id = "syn123")), executed = list(UsedEntity(target_id = "syn456")))) \|> synStore()
Read provenance synGetProvenance(entity) Activity() \|> synGetFromParent(parent = synapse_id)
Remove provenance synDeleteProvenance(entity) synDisassociateActivityFromEntity(Activity, parent = entity)
Get an entity synGet(entity, ...) synGet(synapse_id, file_options = FileOptions(...))
Get a specific version synGet(entity, version = 1) synGet(synapse_id, version_number = 1L)
Skip downloading file content synGet(entity, downloadFile = FALSE) synGet(synapse_id, file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE))
Delete a version only synDelete(obj, version = 1) synDelete(entity, version = 1L, version_only = TRUE)
Query a table synTableQuery(sql) synQuery(sql)
Create a table column synCreateColumn(name = "x", columnType = "STRING") Column(name = "x", column_type = "STRING")
Add a table column manual list manipulation table \|> synAddColumn(Column(name = "x", column_type = "STRING")), then table \|> synStore()
Remove a table column manual list manipulation table \|> synDeleteColumn(name = "x"), then table \|> synStore()
Insert-or-update table rows query, merge, re-store table \|> synUpsertRows(values = df, primary_keys = list("Name"))
Build a table from a CSV, inferring columns synBuildTable(name, parent, "genes.csv") Table(name = ..., parent_id = ...) \|> synStore() \|> synStoreRows(values = "genes.csv", schema_storage_strategy = "INFER_FROM_DATA")

Removed functions

Because 3.0 generates the R layer from the Python models, a 2.x function survives only if the models expose an equivalent. These are the removals most scripts will hit.

Renamed or restructured

  • synBuildTable() → Table(...) |> synStore() |> synStoreRows(values = ..., schema_storage_strategy = "INFER_FROM_DATA"). The table has to exist before rows can be stored into it, so the synStore() step is not optional. See Tables.
  • synTableQuery() → synQuery(). See Tables.
  • synMove() → synGet() |> synSetProperties(parent_id = ...) |> synStore()
  • synGetChildren() → synSyncFromSynapse(recursive = FALSE, download_file = FALSE) and then the container’s $files/$folders, or synWalk() to traverse a whole tree. See Downloading data in bulk.
  • synGetAnnotations() / synSetAnnotations() → the annotations field: read entity$annotations, write synSetProperties(annotations = list(...)) |> synStore(). See Annotations.
  • synGetProvenance() → Activity() |> synGetFromParent(parent = synapse_id), adding parent_version_number for a specific version. See Activity/Provenance.
  • synSetProvenance() / synDeleteProvenance() / synUpdateActivity() → the activity field (an Activity() object) set via synSetProperties(), and synDisassociateActivityFromEntity(Activity, parent = entity) to remove it. See Activity/Provenance.
  • synCreateColumn() / synCreateColumns() / synGetColumn() / synGetColumns() / synGetTableColumns() → the Column() constructor and the table’s own $columns list. See Tables.
  • synCreateSnapshotVersion() → synSnapshot(). See Table.
  • synRestGET() / synRestPOST() / synRestPUT() / synRestDELETE(), and the 2.x synRestGetAsync() family → synRestGet(), synRestPost(), synRestPut(), synRestDelete()
  • synCreateTeam() → Team(name = "...") |> synCreate(); synGetTeam() → Team |> synGetFromId(id = id) or Team |> synGetFromName(name = name); synDeleteTeam() → synDelete(team). See Team.
  • synSendMembershipInvitation() → synInviteToTeam(); synGetTeamOpenInvitations() → synGetOpenInvitations(); synGetMembershipStatus() → synGetUserMembershipStatus(). See Team.
  • synGetUserProfile() → UserProfile |> synGetFromId(user_id = user_id) or UserProfile |> synGetFromUsername(username = username). See UserProfile.
  • Wikis: synGetWiki() → WikiPage(owner_id = ..., id = ...) |> synGet(); storing a wiki page → WikiPage(owner_id = ..., title = ..., markdown = ...) |> synStore(); synGetWikiHeaders() → as.list(WikiHeader() |> synGet(owner_id = ...)); synGetWikiAttachments() → synGetAttachmentHandles(), or synGetAttachment() to fetch one attachment. See Wikis.
  • Evaluations: synGetEvaluation() → Evaluation(id = ...) |> synGet(); synGetEvaluationByName() → Evaluation(name = ...) |> synGet(); synGetEvaluationByContentSource() → synGetEvaluationsByProject(project_id = ...). See Evaluation.
  • Submissions: synSubmit() → Submission(entity_id = ..., evaluation_id = ...) |> synStore(); synGetSubmission() → Submission(id = ...) |> synGet(); synGetSubmissionStatus() → SubmissionStatus(id = ...) |> synGet(), then synStore() to update it; synGetSubmissions() → Submission() |> synGetEvaluationSubmissions(evaluation_id = ...); synGetSubmissionBundles() → SubmissionBundle() |> synGetEvaluationSubmissionBundles(evaluation_id = ...). See Submission.
  • Storage locations: synCreateS3StorageLocation() / synCreateStorageLocationSetting() → StorageLocation(...) |> synStore(); synGetMyStorageLocationSetting() → StorageLocation(storage_location_id = ...) |> synGet(); synSetStorageLocation(), synGetProjectSetting(), and synGetStsStorageToken() keep their names but are now verbs piped from a Folder or Project (folder |> synSetStorageLocation(storage_location_id = ...)). New on the same objects: synDeleteProjectSetting() removes a storage setting, and synIndexFilesForMigration() followed by synMigrateIndexedFiles() moves a container’s existing files to another storage location.
  • Download lists: synGetDownloadList() → synDownloadListFiles(); synGetDownloadListManifest() → synDownloadListManifest(); synRemoveFromDownloadList() → synDownloadListRemove(); synClearDownloadList() → synDownloadListClear(). synDownloadListAdd() is new.

Note the calling convention in the Team, UserProfile, and provenance entries. synGetFromId(), synGetFromName(), synGetFromUsername(), synGetFromParent(), and synDisassociateActivityFromEntity() wrap Python classmethods, so their first argument is the constructor (Team, UserProfile, Activity) — that is what selects the implementation — rather than an instance of it. An empty instance works as the marker too (Team() |> synGetFromId(id = id)), which is the style the reference pages use.

Removed

These 2.x functions have no equivalent in 3.0. Where you still need one, call the REST API directly with synRestGet()/synRestPost()/synRestPut()/synRestDelete():

  • synCreateExternalS3FileHandle(): no replacement.
  • synUploadFileHandle(): no replacement.
  • synDownloadTableColumns(): no replacement. The Python client has deprecated it too, and will remove it in 5.0.0. To download the files in a FILEHANDLEID column, query the table for the file handle IDs and request them from the REST API (POST /fileHandle/batch, with associateObjectType set to TableEntity).
  • synGetConfigFile(): no replacement. Read ~/.synapseConfig directly if you need it. See Configuration.
  • synInvalidateAPIKey(): removed with no replacement. Synapse no longer supports API keys. Use a personal access token instead.

New in 3.0: capabilities that didn’t exist before

The OOP-model generation doesn’t just rename old functions — it also surfaces Python client functionality that synapser never exposed at all. These functions have no 2.x equivalent, so there’s nothing to migrate from, but existing scripts that worked around their absence (manual recursion to bulk update ACLs, hand-rolled directory walks, shelling out to synapseutils from Python) can now be simplified.

Richer access control

synDeletePermissions() and synListAcl() are new. Both work over a single entity or an entire container hierarchy at once, so an audit or cleanup that used to mean writing your own recursive walk over 2.x’s synGetChildren() — and getting the edge cases (nested folders, inherited vs. local ACLs) right yourself — is now one call. dry_run lets you preview exactly what a recursive permissions change will touch before anything is deleted, which matters once you’re operating on an entire project tree instead of a single entity:

# Preview, then perform, a recursive ACL cleardown of a folder and its children
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synDeletePermissions(recursive = TRUE, include_container_content = TRUE, dry_run = TRUE)
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synDeletePermissions(recursive = TRUE, include_container_content = TRUE)

# List every ACL in a hierarchy, optionally as an ASCII tree
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synListAcl(recursive = TRUE, log_tree = TRUE)

synGetPermissions() returns only your own effective permissions. The 2.x reference page documented a principalId argument for it, but 2.x’s function never accepted one, and 3.0 doesn’t either. To check another user’s or team’s permissions, use synGetAcl(principal_id = ...). 2.x also had synGetAcl(); in 3.0 it is a verb you pipe an entity into:

# 2.x
synGetAcl(entity, principal_id = "273948")

# 3.0 -- synGetPermissions() is caller-only; use synGetAcl() for another principal
File(id = "syn123") |> synGetAcl(principal_id = 273948L)

On an Evaluation, synGetAcl() takes no principal_id; it returns the ACL for every principal.

Container traversal and sync

synapser 2.x didn’t include the copy, syncFromSynapse, syncToSynapse, or walk utilities from synapseutils. In 3.0, they are methods on any container, such as a Project or Folder. You can copy a whole tree, download a project to a local folder, upload a directory, or list everything in a hierarchy without downloading it, all with one pipeline in R:

# Recursively copy a folder, and everything in it, to a new parent
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synCopy(parent_id = "syn456")

# Recursively download a folder tree, populating $files/$folders/$tables/...
folder <- Folder(id = "syn123") |> synSyncFromSynapse(path = "~/local-copy")

# Bulk upload: write a manifest that mirrors a local directory, then upload it
folder |> synGenerateSyncManifest(directory_path = "./my_data", manifest_path = "manifest.csv")
folder |> synSyncToSynapse(manifest_path = "manifest.csv")

# Traverse a hierarchy without downloading anything
for (entry in as.list(folder |> synWalk())) {
  dirpath <- entry[[1]]; dirs <- entry[[2]]; nondirs <- entry[[3]]
  cat(dirpath[[1]], "\n")
}

synWalk() returns a GeneratorWrapper — the same lazy-iterator object 2.x returned from synGetChildren(), which no longer exists. Call as.list() on it to materialize every result into a plain list, or nextElem() to pull results one at a time; you can’t loop over it directly the way you can a list. For the narrower job synGetChildren() used to do — listing one container’s immediate children without downloading them — use synSyncFromSynapse(recursive = FALSE, download_file = FALSE) and read the resulting $files/$folders.

The manifest that synGenerateSyncManifest() writes, and that synSyncToSynapse() reads, is the same format that synSyncFromSynapse() and synDownloadListFiles() use — see Manifest CSV and Uploading data in bulk.

JSON Schema binding and validation

Also new: entities can be bound to a JSON Schema and validated against it directly from R. This lets you enforce metadata/annotation standards on Files, Folders, and Tables as part of an R pipeline — catching entities with missing or malformed annotations programmatically instead of relying on manual review or the web UI — and derive annotation values automatically from the schema rather than entering them by hand:

folder <- Folder(id = "syn123")
folder |> synBindSchema(json_schema_uri = "myOrg-mySchema-0.0.1")
folder |> synValidateSchema()
folder |> synUnbindSchema()

synBindSchema() returns the binding record rather than the entity.

This applies to Files, Folders, Tables, Projects, and other container/entity types. Creating the organization and schema themselves uses the new Organization/JSONSchema constructors (SchemaOrganization(), from pre-release 3.0 builds, is now Organization()) — see ?Folder_synBindSchema for a full example. The rest of the family: synGetSchema() and synGetSchemaDerivedKeys() on any bindable entity, plus synGetSchemaValidationStatistics() and synGetInvalidValidation() on containers (Folder, Project).

You can also browse schemas from R. synGetJsonSchemas() lists an organization’s schemas, and synGetVersions() and synGetBody() return a schema’s published versions and its body. synGetAcl() and synUpdateAcl() manage who can publish schemas to an organization:

Organization(name = "myOrg") |> synGetJsonSchemas()

schema <- JSONSchema(organization_name = "myOrg", name = "mySchema")
schema |> synGetVersions()
schema |> synGetBody(version = "0.0.1")

Upserting table rows

synUpsertRows() updates the rows that match on one or more primary-key columns and inserts the rest. In 2.x, you had to query the table, merge the results in R, and store them again. Use dry_run = TRUE to see what would change before writing anything:

table <- Table(id = "syn123") |> synGet()
table |> synUpsertRows(values = df, primary_keys = list("Name"), dry_run = TRUE)
table |> synUpsertRows(values = df, primary_keys = list("Name"))

See Tables for the full set of options.

More synapseutils utilities

3.0 also adds three more synapseutils utilities that 2.x didn’t include: changing a file’s metadata, copying a wiki, and migrating files to another storage location.

# Rename a file, or change its download name or content type, without
# re-uploading it. These fields can't be changed with synStore().
synGet("syn123", file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE)) |>
  synChangeMetadata(name = "renamed.csv", download_as = "renamed.csv", content_type = "text/csv")

# Copy a project's whole wiki tree to another entity and rewrite internal links.
# Set `id` to copy only the sub-tree under that page.
WikiPage(owner_id = "syn123") |> synCopy(destination_owner_id = "syn456")

# Move a container's existing files to another storage location in two steps
folder <- Folder(id = "syn123")
folder |> synIndexFilesForMigration(dest_storage_location_id = "12345", db_path = "migration.db")
folder |> synMigrateIndexedFiles(db_path = "migration.db", force = TRUE)

synMigrateIndexedFiles() asks for confirmation before it moves anything. When it can’t ask (for example, in an R script), it stops without migrating unless you pass force = TRUE.

Wiki history and page order

2.x could get and store a wiki page, but not its history or its order in the wiki navigation. In 3.0, you can list a page’s versions, restore an earlier version, and set the order of the pages:

# List a page's versions, then restore one of them
WikiHistorySnapshot() |> synGet(owner_id = "syn123", id = wiki_id)
WikiPage(owner_id = "syn123", id = wiki_id, wiki_version = "0") |> synRestore()

# Set the order of the wiki's pages in the navigation.
# Page IDs are numeric strings, such as "12345", not numbers.
WikiOrderHint(owner_id = "syn123") |> synGet() |>
  synSetProperties(id_list = list(root_id, page_2_id, page_1_id)) |>
  synStore()

# Download a page's markdown
WikiPage(owner_id = "syn123", id = wiki_id) |> synGetMarkdownFile(download_location = "~/temp")

synGetAttachmentPreview() downloads the preview of an attachment. See Wikis.

Evaluation queues, submissions, and teams

The Python client added several functions for running an evaluation queue (a challenge) that 2.x never had:

# Count a queue's submissions without downloading them
synGetSubmissionCount(evaluation_id = "9614112")

# Update up to 500 submission statuses in one request, instead of one
# synStore() call each
synBatchUpdateSubmissionStatuses(evaluation_id = "9614112", statuses = statuses)

# Cancel one of your own submissions
Submission(id = submission_id) |> synCancel()

# List the queues you can submit to
synGetAvailableEvaluations(active_only = TRUE)

# Withdraw a pending team invitation (2.x could send one, but not delete it)
invitations <- Team(id = 123456L) |> synGet() |> synGetOpenInvitations()
synDeleteInvitation(invitation_id = invitations[[1]]$id)

See Evaluation, Submission and Team.

Synapse AI agents

Agent and AgentSession let you chat with a Synapse AI agent from R. Agent() with no arguments uses the same default agent as the Synapse chat page. A session starts automatically the first time you send a prompt:

agent <- Agent()
agent |> synPrompt(prompt = "What is in the AD Knowledge Portal?", print_response = TRUE)
agent |> synGetChatHistory()

To use a custom agent, register it with synRegister() (custom agents are available only to Sage Bionetworks staff). To manage sessions yourself, use AgentSession() |> synStart(). See Agent.

Known pitfall: integer literals

R’s bare numeric literals (1) are doubles. Parameters the Synapse API expects as integers — version_number, version, row IDs/versions in synDeleteRows(df = ...) — must use the L suffix (1L). Passing 1 instead of 1L can produce unexpected behavior or an API error. This isn’t new in 3.0, but it surfaces more often now that raw integer parameters are exposed directly instead of being hidden behind wrapper defaults.

  • Configuration covers the .synapseConfig file and client settings.
  • Troubleshooting covers common connection and configuration errors.
  • System Dependencies covers the system libraries needed on Linux and the supported Python versions.

Reference:

  • The reference site is organized per entity type (File, Table, Folder, …) — every constructor and method function is documented there, generated directly from the Python client so it stays current going forward.
